examples.ko: 저는 교장실에 가 본 적이 한 번도 없어요.
examples.en: I have never been to the principal's office.

examples.ko: 교장실은 이 층 복도 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The principal's office is at the end of the second-floor hallway.
The teacher took the documents to the principal's office.

examples.ko: 교장실 앞에서 떨려서 한참 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was nervous and stood in front of the principal's office for a long time.
Where is the principal's office?

examples.ko: 상을 받은 날 교장실에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On the day I won the prize, we took a photo in the principal's office.

explain: 학교 교장 선생님의 방이에요. 선생님들이 모여 있는 곳은 '교무실'이라서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is the room of the school principal. It is easy to confuse with '교무실', the staff room where teachers gather.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 도둑질을 하면 안 된다고 배웠어요.
examples.en: As a child I learned that stealing is wrong.
Theft is a serious crime, so you get punished.

examples.ko: 가게에서 도둑질이 자주 일어나서 카메라를 달았어요.
examples.en: Thefts kept happening in the shop, so they installed a camera.

examples.ko: 도둑질로 잡혀 간 사람이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A person arrested for theft appeared on the news.
The villagers are anxious because of the thefts.
The punishment for theft is very strict.

explain: 행동은 '도둑질', 사람은 '도둑'이에요. 도둑에게 물건을 빼앗긴 쪽은 '도둑을 맞다', '도둑맞다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: The act is '도둑질' and the person is '도둑'. Someone whose things were taken by a thief says '도둑을 맞다' or '도둑맞다'.

examples.en: Breathe in deeply and then breathe out slowly.
If you breathe in through your nose, you feel calmer.
The doctor told me to breathe in.
I feel good breathing in the clean air.
When you're nervous, try breathing in deeply.
Your belly comes out when you breathe in.

explain: 반대말 '내쉬다'와 짝으로 '숨을 들이쉬고 내쉬세요'라고 말해요. 병원이나 운동할 때 많이 들어요. 공기뿐 아니라 물이나 음료를 마실 때는 '들이마시다'를 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with its opposite '내쉬다' in '숨을 들이쉬고 내쉬세요', which you hear at clinics and in exercise classes. For drinking liquids, use '들이마시다' instead.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 허리 라인이 예뻐 보여요.
examples.en: This outfit makes the waistline look nice.
I stand at the starting line and wait for the signal.

examples.ko: 회사에서 새 라인 제품을 곧 내놓을 거예요.
examples.en: The company will soon release a new product line.

examples.ko: 턱 라인이 깔끔해 보이는 머리 모양이에요.
examples.en: It's a hairstyle that makes the jawline look neat.

examples.ko: 이 라인 뒤에 한 줄로 서 주세요.
examples.en: Please line up in one row behind this line.

examples.ko: 그림에서 라인을 굵게 그리면 더 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: If you draw the lines thick in a picture, they stand out more.

explain: 줄, 선, 몸의 윤곽, 상품 종류까지 쓰임이 넓어요. '허리 라인', '턱 라인'처럼 몸 모양을 말할 때 자주 써요. 지하철 노선은 '2호선'처럼 '선'으로 말해요.
explain_en: It covers lines, outlines, body contours, and product ranges. It is common for body shape, as in 허리 라인 and 턱 라인. Subway routes are called by '선', as in 2호선.

p.n: 선 is the neutral everyday word; 라인 sounds like a design, sports or fashion line.

examples.en: Take care so you do not catch a cold.
I learned that taking care of yourself is the most important thing.

examples.ko: 요즘 감기가 유행이라서 몸조심하면서 지내고 있어요.
examples.en: Colds are going around, so I am taking care of myself.
In winter you have to take extra care of yourself.
Take care not to get sick and have a good trip.
I told my pregnant friend to take care of herself.

explain: 헤어질 때 '몸조심하세요', '건강하세요'처럼 인사로도 써요. 친구에게는 '몸조심해'라고 말해요. 아픈 사람에게 하는 '빨리 나으세요'와는 쓰는 상황이 달라요.
explain_en: It works as a goodbye greeting, like '몸조심하세요' or '건강하세요'. To a friend you say '몸조심해'. It is used in different situations from '빨리 나으세요', which you say to someone who is sick.

examples.en: The child came running at the mother's call.
I was called by the teacher and went to the staff room.
I heard the call but pretended I didn't.
That song sounded like a call from home.
It was an urgent call, so I hurried out.
I went outside because my friend called me.

explain: '부르다'의 명사형이에요. '부름을 받다'는 격식 있는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '불러서 갔어요'처럼 동사로 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is the noun form of '부르다'. '부름을 받다' is formal; in everyday talk people usually use the verb, as in '불러서 갔어요'.

examples.en: There is a shovel in the garden.
My father dug the ground with a shovel.
We took shovels and cleared the snow.
Please keep the shovel in the storage room.
A lot of dirt stuck to the shovel.
I can lend you a shovel too, if you need.

explain: '삽으로 땅을 파다'처럼 '파다'와 자주 써요. 작은 화분용은 '모종삽'이라고 불러요. '삽질'은 쓸데없이 고생했다는 뜻의 속어로도 써요.

phrases.en: I wasted effort all night and have nothing to show for it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸데없는 일에 힘만 들이고 소득이 없을 때 쓰는 속어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slang for working hard on something that leads nowhere.

explain_en: It often goes with '파다', as in '삽으로 땅을 파다'. A small garden trowel is a '모종삽'. '삽질' is also slang for doing a lot of work for nothing.

examples.en: Please mix lowercase letters and numbers in your password.

examples.ko: 이 칸에는 소문자만 입력할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only enter lowercase letters in this box.
Please write in lowercase, not capitals.
Lowercase letters are smaller than capital letters.
a is a lowercase letter and A is a capital letter.
The message my friend sent is all in lowercase.

explain: 반대말은 '대문자'예요. 영어에서는 문장의 첫 글자와 이름을 대문자로 쓰고, 나머지는 보통 소문자로 써요. 한글에는 대문자와 소문자 구분이 없어서 영어 같은 알파벳 글자를 이야기할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is 대문자 (uppercase). In English you capitalize the first letter of a sentence and names, and write the rest in lowercase. Hangul has no uppercase/lowercase distinction, so this word is used when talking about the English alphabet and other Latin letters.

examples.en: I lost my wallet, so I reported it to the police.
When you move, you have to report your new address to the community center.

examples.ko: 해외에서 사 온 물건은 공항에서 신고해요.
examples.en: You declare things you bought abroad at the airport.
If you see an accident on the road, call 112 right away.

examples.ko: 이 문제를 신고하려면 어디로 전화해야 해요?
examples.en: Where do I call to report this problem?
I didn't know how to report it, so I looked it up online.

explain: '신고하다'는 경찰·구청·세관처럼 기관에 알려야 할 일에만 써요. 친구나 가족에게 알릴 때는 '알리다', '말하다'를 써요. 이사 뒤에 주소를 알리는 건 '전입 신고를 하다'라는 정해진 말이 있어요.
explain_en: 신고하다 is only for telling an official body such as the police, a district office or customs. To tell friends or family, use '알리다' or '말하다'. Reporting your new address after a move has a fixed phrase, '전입 신고를 하다'.

examples.en: The afternoon class starts at two.
It's hard to get up in the morning, so I signed up for the afternoon class.
Friends in the afternoon class go home in the evening.
I'm in the afternoon class, so I go to the academy after lunch.
Does the tuition change if I switch to the afternoon class?
The afternoon class teacher is different from the morning class teacher.

explain: 점심 이후 시간에 하는 반이에요. 반대말은 '오전반'이고 '저녁반'과도 나눠서 말해요. 학원 등록할 때 시간대를 고르는 말로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a class held after lunch. The opposite is '오전반', and it's also distinguished from '저녁반'. It is often used when choosing a time slot while registering at an academy.

examples.en: I didn't feel well, so I went to the infirmary.
The infirmary nurse gave me medicine.

examples.ko: 의무실은 일 층 복도 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The infirmary is at the end of the first-floor hallway.

examples.ko: 넘어져서 무릎을 다쳤으니 의무실로 가 보세요.
examples.en: You fell and hurt your knee, so go to the infirmary.

examples.ko: 죄송한데요, 이 건물 의무실이 어디에 있어요?
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the infirmary in this building?

examples.ko: 의무실에서 열을 재 보니 조금 높았어요.
examples.en: I took my temperature at the infirmary and it was a little high.

explain: 회사, 군대, 공장처럼 사람이 많이 모인 곳에서 아픈 사람을 돌보는 방이에요. 학교에서는 보통 '보건실'이라고 해요. '의무실에 가다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a room for looking after sick people in places with many people, such as companies, the military and factories. In schools it is usually called '보건실'. You say '의무실에 가다'.

examples.en: I read a magazine in the hospital waiting room.

examples.ko: 이 잡지책은 매달 첫째 주에 나와요.
examples.en: This magazine comes out in the first week of every month.

examples.ko: 서점에서 패션 잡지책을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a fashion magazine at the bookstore.
The photos in the magazine are so pretty.
Magazines are piled up on the desk.

examples.ko: 이번 달 잡지책에 제 글이 실렸어요.
examples.en: My writing was published in this month's magazine.

explain: '잡지'와 같은 뜻이에요. 보통 '잡지를 읽다'처럼 쓰고, 종이로 된 것을 말할 때 '잡지책'이라고도 해요. 정기적으로 나오는 것은 '월간지', '주간지'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It means the same as '잡지'. People usually say '잡지를 읽다', and '잡지책' is also used for the printed paper version. Regularly published ones are called '월간지' (monthly) or '주간지' (weekly).

examples.ko: 월별 방문자 그래프에 점선으로 평균선을 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please add the average line as a dotted line on the monthly visitors graph.
Please cut the paper along the dotted line.

examples.ko: 점선이 끝나는 곳에 이름을 써 주세요.
examples.en: Please write your name where the dotted line ends.
On the map, the dotted line shows the border.

examples.ko: 점선 부분은 아직 공사 중인 길이에요.
examples.en: The dotted part is a road that is still under construction.
Don't write anything in the dotted box.

explain: 끊기지 않은 '실선'과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. 서류에서 '점선을 따라 자르세요', '점선 위에 서명하세요'처럼 안내문에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It helps to remember it as the pair of '실선', the unbroken line. It often appears in instructions on forms, like '점선을 따라 자르세요' or '점선 위에 서명하세요'.

examples.en: The road is slippery, so walk slowly and be careful.
I'm always careful not to catch a cold.
You must be especially careful when driving.
If you pay attention to spelling, you make far fewer mistakes.
I'm being careful not to fall on the stairs.

examples.ko: 도서관에서는 큰 소리로 말하지 않도록 주의했어요.
examples.en: I was careful not to talk loudly in the library.

explain: 친구에게는 '조심해요'라고 하고, '주의하세요'는 안내방송이나 경고문처럼 조금 격식 있는 곳에서 많이 들려요. 안내문에는 '미끄럼 주의', '화기 주의'처럼 '하다' 없이 명사로도 써요. 조심할 대상은 '~에 주의하다'로 받아요.
explain_en: To a friend you say '조심해요'. 주의하세요 is what you hear in announcements and on warning signs, so it sounds a bit more formal. Signs often use the noun alone, like '미끄럼 주의' (caution: slippery). The thing to watch takes 에: '~에 주의하다'.
